q: How much husk would an economiser save in a Bargarh rice mill boiler?
title: Bargarh rice mill economiser: husk saved
short: About a tenth of your husk. TERI's rule of thumb: every 6 degrees of feedwater preheat saves 1% of fuel, and preheating to 90 degrees with better condensate return saves about 10%. For a 2 tph Bargarh mill burning 1,610 t of husk a year, that is about 160 t.
audience: Owners of small and medium parboiling mills in Bargarh weighing a boiler upgrade or loan

sections.h: Why the boiler is the place to start
p: Most Bargarh mills run three-pass husk boilers of about 4 tph at 10 kg/cm2, with no economiser beyond a locally made feedwater preheater and no instruments except a pressure gauge. Steam goes to hot water for soaking, direct steaming and the paddy dryer, so every percent of boiler loss shows up as husk you could have sold.

ul: About 86 small and medium mills could fit waste heat recovery on their boilers.
Together they would save about 16,900 t of husk a year (5,070 toe), worth about Rs 20.3 million at the husk selling price.
Solar water heaters for soaking water would save about 20,000 t more.
Only 3 mills above 10 tph have cogeneration; the other 6 large mills could add about 6 MW.

sections.h: What it does for your carbon number
p: Little, honestly. Husk CO2 is biogenic, so burning less husk barely moves the fossil figure a buyer sees; your grid kWh does that. The economiser's case is money: husk freed for sale, and steam you can measure. If you want the fossil line to fall too, pair it with efficient motors, plastic elevator buckets and pump upgrades.
